name: Syncope (Medicine)
overview: Syncope (Medicine) is a health topic that clinicians and patients frequently discuss during care planning in India and worldwide. Key considerations include transient loss of consciousness and postural tone. This summary is educational and should be paired with professional medical evaluation.
possibleCauses: Health professionals note that syncope, commonly known as fainting or passing out, is a loss of consciousness and muscle strength characterized by a fast onset, short duration...
From a clinical perspective, it is caused by a decrease in blood flow to the brain, typically from low blood pressure.
From a clinical perspective, there are sometimes symptoms before the loss of consciousness such as lightheadedness, sweating, pale skin, blurred vision, nausea, vomiting, or feeling warm.
In routine practice, syncope may also be associated with a short episode of muscle twitching.
In routine practice, psychiatric causes can also be determined when a patient experiences fear, anxiety, or panic.
